subject: Proposal: Dedicated GPU pool + migration credit — request for exec approval
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Amelia Barnes <amelia@novum.ai>
Cc: Jacob Chen <jacob.chen@novum.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated GPU pool + migration proposal (Novum AI)

Hi Amelia / Jacob,

Thanks again for the time last week — appreciate the洞 deep dive on your inference mix and seasonal batch spikes. Per our conversation, attached is a focused proposal for a Dedicated GPU pool sized for your 95th-percentile throughput with an optional migration credit to offset switching costs. High-level summary below: 

- Configuration: 8x A100-equivalent accelerator nodes (32GB) in a single-region pool; autoscale-burst to add 2x nodes for 90s windows.
- Throughput SLO: 99th percentile token latency target at 75ms for 512-token requests at baseline traffic.
- Commit: 12 month reserved capacity (monthly billing) with option to prepay 1 month as onboarding credit.
- Pricing: list price $220k/month; proposed customer price $176k/month (20% standard strategic discount).
- Migration credit: proposed one-time credit equal to 2 months of committed spend (applied as account credit over first 90 days) to cover integration and performance tuning risk.

Attachments: [Attachment: Novum_Redwood_Proposal_v2.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)]

Questions for you: does the sizing and SLO align with your internal perf targets? Are you able to review the contractual term that allows a 30-day validation window post-onboard?

If this looks close, I can run this by Finance and request an executive approval path for the migration credit — otherwise we can tighten the commit or shorten the tie-to-term to reduce the credit ask.

Thanks,

Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0172
From: Amelia Barnes <amelia@novum.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jacob Chen <jacob.chen@novum.ai>, procurement@novum.ai
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU pool + migration proposal (Novum AI)

Diego — thank you for the fast turn. A few quick notes after we reviewed with the infra and finance teams:

- Sizing: 8 nodes + burst sounds right for now, but we need a hard throughput guarantee for peak windows (we'll need a written SLO and a credits policy if you miss it).
- Price: the 20% discount is helpful but we have competing offers from two vendors that are ~15% lower after their first-year credits.
- Migration risk: the team is asking for stronger onboarding assurances. Instead of a 2-month credit, would you consider 3 months or a phased credit tied to milestones (e.g., validation + production cutover)?

We'd prefer to keep negotiations at the AE/manager level but this migration credit number is outside our standard procurement threshold — would you be able to loop in someone who can approve additional credits if necessary?

If you can send a revised structure that includes an SLO with a credits table and a phased migration credit, we can move to an LOI quickly.

Regards,

Amelia Barnes
Head of Procurement
Novum AI
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 08:05:00 -0800
Subject: FWD: Novum AI — request for 3-month migration credit + SLO (need exec approval)

Team — forwarding Novum's reply. They have a strong competitive alternative and want: 

1) an explicit throughput SLO (99th p token latency) + a credits table if we miss it
2) a 3-month migration credit, preferably phased (validation -> prod cutover)
3) willingness to sign LOI quickly if we bridge the onboarding risk

Deal metrics: ARR run-rate on proposed pricing = $2.112M/year (12mo commit). CAC/contract uplift looks attractive; strategic customer (AI SaaS platform) — good reference potential.

Suggested concession path (one of):
- Option A (manager-level): 2 months migration credit + 10% additional off first 3 months (no additional exec signoff)
- Option B (exec-level): 3 months migration credit phased (1 month on validation, 2 months on production) + 15% off first quarter (requires exec/finance approval)

I've attached our deal analytics (traffic profile + forecast) to justify sizing. If we go Option B I recommend we ask for a 15% committed uplift in year 2 pricing protection clause to preserve unit economics.

Attachments: [Attachment: deal-analytics-20261125.csv (CSV, 32KB)]

Can you confirm what level of credit/discount we can approve? I can draft the milestone language for the SLO credits table.

Thanks,

Diego
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FWD: Novum AI — request for 3-month migration credit + SLO (need exec approval)

Diego — thanks for the context and the analytics. Quick read: this is a strategic logo with reference value and a healthy committed ARR, so discounts here are defensible with the right guardrails.

I can approve Option A immediately (2 months migration credit + additional 10% off the first 3 months) from a commercial perspective. For Option B (3 months migration credit + 15% off Q1), we need one level up — looping Marcus for final sign-off because that has greater revenue impact and touches finance. Marcus, can you review the numbers and confirm if Finance can accept a phased credit treatment that amortizes over 90 days and is reflected as account credit (not cash rebate)? Also include Legal (Laura) to finalize the SLO credit table language and any addenda for onboarding acceptance tests.

A couple of guardrails to recommend in the SLO credits table: 
- Credits only trigger after a 30-day validation window post-cutover.
- Max quarterly credit cap at 20% of committed monthly spend.
- Phased credit only applied if customer completes the agreed validation checklist and traffic profile is within +/-15% of the forecast attached.

Diego — draft a quick LOI that captures Option A so we can keep momentum while Marcus reviews Option B.

Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Amelia Barnes <amelia@novum.ai>
Cc: Jacob Chen <jacob.chen@novum.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 17:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU pool + migration proposal (Novum AI)

Amelia — appreciate the quick turnaround. Per internal review we can offer an interim structure to move forward while we finalize exec approval for the larger credit: 

Interim (manager-approved) offer — Option A: 
- Commit: 12 months dedicated pool (8 nodes)
- Price: $158.4k/month (20% off list + extra 10% on first 3 months)
- Migration credit: 2 months of committed spend applied as account credit over the first 90 days
- SLO/credits: we will include a 99th percentile token latency SLO with a credits table. Credits are subject to the 30-day validation window and a quarterly credit cap of 20% of monthly committed spend.

We are also escalating Option B to Marcus and Finance for consideration (3-month phased credit + 15% off Q1). Marcus and Laura are cc'ed on this thread — we'll share a short LOI link below that captures Option A so you can sign and we can begin onboarding in parallel while the exec committee reviews Option B.

LOI: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/novum-loi-1187
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/48572/DEAL-1187

If you sign Option A by EOD Friday we can guarantee a Dec 14 onboard start and a Jan 4 production cutover target. Let me know a good time for a 30-minute exec alignment call this week if Novum wants to push for Option B ahead of signature.

Best,

Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Novum_Redwood_Proposal_v2.pdf]
